It would be extremely helpful if the 24-hour sign were removed and a sign with the hours displayed, since the clinic is no longer open 24 hours a day! We wasted half an hour with our suffering dog, thinking someone would open the door for us.

On Saturday morning, my partner and I took our dog to this veterinary clinic by appointment because of inflamed, bleeding gums and obvious pain. The doctor who examined him diagnosed severe periodontitis with gingival hyperemia and prescribed an antibiotic (Stomorgyl 2), with instructions to administer one tablet daily for 10 days. We were also told that the medical records would be emailed to us immediately.
On Saturday afternoon, we went to the pharmacy to pick up the medication, which was not in stock at the time, and picked it up on Sunday. Reading the package insert, we realized that the prescribed formulation called for one tablet per 2 kg of body weight for 6-10 days. Considering that our dog weighs 8.5 kg, the prescribed dosage was clearly incorrect.
On Monday morning, my partner called the clinic for clarification. The vet who answered suggested that her colleague had probably misprescribed the medication and that perhaps she should have written Stomorgyl 20. My partner pointed out that our dog weighs 8.5 kilos, and he responded by saying, "Then maybe it should have been Stomorgyl 10." My partner asked if she could look at the medical records (which she never received) to determine the correct dosage, but the vet, rather rudely, replied that he couldn't and that we would be contacted. Receiving no further response, my partner called back late in the morning. A second, more friendly vet quickly dismissed her concern, assuring her that the doctor (whose name we didn't know, as she hadn't even signed the prescription or sent us the records) would send us the correct prescription at 2:30 PM sharp.
At around 4:00 PM, having still not received anything, my partner went to the clinic in person, where the doctor who had examined the dog was present. The doctor stated that she hadn't been informed of anything, that she had just arrived (only to contradict herself later, saying she had arrived at the clinic and had been busy with visits), that perhaps she had made a mistake, but that the mistake could have been made because—and I quote—"there are many dosages of that drug." She even went so far as to suggest that we could adjust our dosages ourselves by increasing the number of pills from 1 to 4 per day. My partner pointed out that it was absurd to give the dog 4 pills instead of 1, and that in any case the package contained 20 pills and therefore wouldn't be enough to complete the treatment. She also pointed out that she was the veterinarian and that she was responsible for the prescriptions.
The doctor gave my partner the correct prescription, glossing over the request for the medical records. My partner again urged her to hand it over, and in the end the doctor had to write it on the spot, backdating it to Saturday, June 6th. This record had never been sent to us because it had never been written on Saturday.
These are our observations:
1) This doctor, who we later learned was Laura Paris, gave absolutely no thought to the seriousness of what had happened. If she had mistakenly written Stomorgyl 20 instead of 2 or 10, and we hadn't read the package insert, we would have given our 8.5-kilo dog the recommended dose for a 20-kilo dog.
2) There was no attention paid to us. We had to call several times and go in person to get confirmation.
3) We paid a high consultation fee for a service of unspeakable quality.
4) If what the doctor said is true—that she wasn't informed—it's serious that in a veterinary facility, there's no exchange of information, despite repeated phone calls and the assurances we'd receive "everything" by 2:30 PM.

I won't add anything else.

I took my Labrador to this clinic a few days ago to request a quote for the removal of a recurrence of a small mast cell tumor (which had already been operated on at this clinic).
I had an appointment with Dr. Sisini, but after a bit of a wait, I found another surgeon, who examined my dog.
After the visit, we agreed that he would send me a quote for pre-operative tests and the surgery.
Today, having not received a quote, I decided to call.
The secretary answered and told me that Dr. Sisini won't operate on my dog.
Shocked, I asked why and was told he didn't know, and with a quick goodbye, hung up.
I called back demanding to know why... I was told that they no longer perform oncology surgery.
I insisted that the other surgeon told me they would do it.
At this point, Sisini responded, saying they only do orthopedic surgery.
But that's not the case, since he himself operated on my dog ​​two years ago for the same problem.
He rudely told me to go to the San Siro Clinic, where he's already being treated by an oncologist.
I found Dr. Sisini completely unprofessional, because if I hadn't asked for the estimate I was waiting for, I still wouldn't have known he wouldn't have operated on my dog.
At this point, I advise against the clinic, due to its unreliability, lack of willingness to provide explanations, and lack of professionalism.
Avoid this clinic. Dr. Sisinni was unsympathetic and unprofessional. If you love your pets, I recommend taking them to other clinics.

Dear Massimo,

We sincerely thank you for giving us your 5-star rating. Knowing we've left a good impression is a great satisfaction for us and an important confirmation of the work we do every day with passion and dedication.

Thank you for your trust. We will always be happy to welcome you and your four-legged friend with the same attention and professionalism.

Warmest regards from all the staff at the Maciachini Veterinary Clinic. 🐾

Your appreciation is very important to us and represents valuable recognition of the commitment our entire staff dedicates every day to caring for our patients and supporting their families.

Thank you for your trust in us. We hope to welcome you back to the clinic, again for routine checkups and with your four-legged friend in excellent health.

Warmest regards from all the staff at the Maciachini Veterinary Clinic. 🐾
Terrible experience. The doctor was brusque and lacking in empathy. Definitely the first and last time.

Dr. Sisinni operated on both knees of my dog ​​(a Maremma-Bernese mix) in a short period of time, about 10 years ago. He had torn his cruciate ligaments and also the meniscus on one knee. He performed the surgery using a relatively new technique at the time, straightening the bones and inserting plates. Paco is now 14 years old, and I recently had him x-rayed in Croatia to assess the extent of his arthritis (which is common for an older dog). I received answers about his arthritis and compliments on the knee replacement, which is still in perfect condition.
I sincerely thank Dr. Sisinni for giving my friend Paco a beautiful life.
Unfortunately they no longer offer 24/7 assistance, but they are still professional
Terrible experience. If you care about your animals, don't bring them here.
